children: Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar in early trade, but may be weighed by ongoing tensions in the Middle East. "The U.S. struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iran retaliated against bases hosting U.S. forces in Jordan, with additional incidents reported around the UAE and the Strait of Hormuz," NAB's Rodrigo Catril says in commentary. The rise in oil prices triggers risk-off sentiment, the senior FX strategist adds. The U.S. dollar is little changed at 159.70 yen and is 0.1% higher at 1,367.90 won, while the Australian dollar is 0.1% higher at US$0.7174, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
